title: Roger Sperry, Michael Gazzaniga & Francis Crick's Final Quest (1913–1994 / 1939– / 1916–2004) — Upside-Down Newt Eyes, Caltech's Split-Brain 'Left-Hemisphere Interpreter,' and Crick & Koch's 28-Year Assault on the Neural Correlates of Consciousness

teenKit.tldr: Over 80 years, scientists like Roger Sperry, Michael Gazzaniga, and Francis Crick cracked how your brain physically wires itself in the womb and splits your consciousness into halves.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding the physical basis of consciousness helps us solve severe neurological disorders, brain injuries, and unlocks the ultimate mystery of what makes you, you.
keyTakeaways: Roger Sperry proved that neurons find their exact targets during development using chemical signposts rather than random trial-and-error.
Split-brain experiments revealed that the left and right hemispheres of the brain can operate almost like two independent minds inside one skull.
The left-hemisphere 'interpreter' constantly invents plausible stories to explain why your body does things, even when it has no idea of the real cause.

vocab.meaning: The rule that growing nerve fibers use specific chemical molecular tags to find and connect to their exact targets in the brain.
Surgical cutting of the thick cable of nerve fibers connecting the left and right brain hemispheres, mostly used to stop severe epilepsy.
A storytelling function in the left brain that constantly spins a narrative to make sense of your actions and the world around you.
The absolute minimum physical brain activity and structure necessary to experience a specific conscious thought or feeling.

quiz.question: What happens when you rotate a newt's eye 180 degrees when it is young, according to Roger Sperry's work?
options: The newt's brain adapts instantly and learns to see normally.
The newt strikes backward at flies because its optic nerve wires back to its original directional targets using chemical tags.
The newt goes completely blind permanently because the eye tissue dies.
The newt's eye rotates back to its original position on its own.
quiz.explanation: Chemical guidance cues force the regenerating optic nerve fibers to reconnect to their original physical coordinates, making the newt see the world upside down and backwards.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of the 'Left-Hemisphere Interpreter' discovered by Gazzaniga and LeDoux?
options: Translating foreign languages into English instantly.
Controlling the physical movement of the left side of the body.
Inventing logical, smooth stories to explain why the body is performing certain behaviors, even if it doesn't know the real reason.
Processing raw visual data coming from both eyes simultaneously.
quiz.explanation: The left hemisphere hates chaos and will instantly fabricate a confident, believable explanation for any action, even actions commanded secretly to the isolated right brain.

quiz.question: What was Francis Crick's major shift in focus later in his career?
options: Abandoning biology entirely to study astrophysics and black holes.
Teaming up with Christof Koch to turn the elusive mystery of human consciousness into a concrete, experimental science.
Inventing the first commercial functional MRI machine for hospitals.
Proving that DNA molecules can think on their own.
quiz.explanation: After co-discovering the structure of DNA, Crick spent decades trying to map the exact neural correlates of consciousness in the mammalian brain.

And would their left hemisphere interpreters invent a single, shared eye? That is something to really think about. Keep questioning the reality your brain presents to you.
